import pandas as pd

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_95/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_95/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_95/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_95/training_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_95/training_4.csv"
source5_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_95/training_5.csv"
source6_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_95/training_6.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'] (92 rows)
df5 = pd.read_csv(source5_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike']
df6 = pd.read_csv(source6_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']

# Step 1: JOIN : [["Source6_95_0", "Source6_95_2"], ["batsman", "batsman"]]
join_0_2 = pd.merge(df0, df2, on="batsman", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Step 2: JOIN : [["Source6_95_1", "Source6_95_3"], ["batsman", "batsman"]]
join_1_3 = pd.merge(df1, df3, on="batsman", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Step 3: JOIN : [["Source6_95_4", "Source6_95_6"], ["batsman", "batsman"]]
join_4_6 = pd.merge(df4, df6, on="batsman", suffixes=('_x_5', '_y_7'))

# Step 4: Group by batsman with specified aggregations
# Aggregations:
# sum(Source6_95_0.total_runs) -> from df0
# sum(Source6_95_1.batsman_runs) -> from df1
# sum(Source6_95_2.total_runs) -> from df2
# sum(Source6_95_3.batsman_runs) -> from df3
# avg(Source6_95_4.batsman_runs) -> from df4
# sum(Source6_95_5.no of balls) -> from df5
# sum(Source6_95_5.batsman_runs) -> from df5
# avg(Source6_95_5.strike) -> from df5
# sum(Source6_95_6.batsman_runs) -> from df6

# To do this, we need to join all sources on batsman first, then aggregate.

# Join all sources on batsman stepwise:

# Join join_0_2 with join_1_3 on batsman
join_0_2_1_3 = pd.merge(join_0_2, join_1_3, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Join the above with df5 on batsman
join_all_except_4_6 = pd.merge(join_0_2_1_3, df5, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Join the above with join_4_6 on batsman
full_join = pd.merge(join_all_except_4_6, join_4_6, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Now perform group by batsman with aggregations
agg_dict = {
    'total_runs_x': 'sum',          # from df0 (join_0_2)
    'batsman_runs_x': 'sum',        # from df1 (join_1_3)
    'total_runs_y': 'sum',          # from df2 (join_0_2)
    'batsman_runs_y': 'sum',        # from df3 (join_1_3)
    'batsman_runs_x_5': 'mean',     # from df4 (join_4_6)
    'no of balls': 'sum',           # from df5
    'batsman_runs_y_7': 'sum',      # from df5 (batsman_runs) + join_4_6 suffix? careful
    'strike': 'mean',               # from df5
    'batsman_runs': 'sum'           # from df6 (join_4_6)
}

# But note columns in full_join:
# From join_0_2: total_runs_x (df0), total_runs_y (df2)
# From join_1_3: batsman_runs_x (df1), batsman_runs_y (df3)
# From df5: no of balls, batsman_runs, strike
# From join_4_6: batsman_runs_x_5 (df4), batsman_runs_y_7 (df6)

# So columns in full_join are:
# batsman
# total_runs_x (df0)
# total_runs_y (df2)
# batsman_runs_x (df1)
# batsman_runs_y (df3)
# no of balls (df5)
# batsman_runs (df5)
# strike (df5)
# batsman_runs_x_5 (df4)
# batsman_runs_y_7 (df6)

# We need to confirm the column names in full_join:

# The join_4_6 merge used suffixes=('_x_5', '_y_7'):
# So df4.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x_5
# df6.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_y_7

# The join_0_2 merge used suffixes=('_x', '_y'):
# df0.total_runs -> total_runs_x
# df2.total_runs -> total_runs_y

# The join_1_3 merge used suffixes=('_x', '_y'):
# df1.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x
# df3.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_y

# df5 columns: no of balls, batsman_runs, strike

# So the agg_dict is correct.

# Perform aggregation:
result = full_join.groupby('batsman', as_index=False).agg({
    'total_runs_x': 'sum',
    'batsman_runs_x': 'sum',
    'total_runs_y': 'sum',
    'batsman_runs_y': 'sum',
    'batsman_runs_x_5': 'mean',
    'no of balls': 'sum',
    'batsman_runs_y_7': 'sum',
    'strike': 'mean',
    'batsman_runs': 'sum'
})

# Ensure column types match target schema:
# Target Schema:
# ['batsman': string,
#  'batsman_runs_x': float,
#  'total_runs_x': integer,
#  'total_runs_y': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_y': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_x_5': integer,
#  'no of balls': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_y_7': integer,
#  'strike': float,
#  'batsman_runs': integer]

# Convert types accordingly:

result['batsman'] = result['batsman'].astype(str)
result['batsman_runs_x'] = result['batsman_runs_x'].astype(float)
result['total_runs_x'] = result['total_runs_x'].fillna(0).astype(int)
result['total_runs_y'] = result['total_runs_y'].fillna(0).astype(int)
result['batsman_runs_y'] = result['batsman_runs_y'].fillna(0).astype(int)
# batsman_runs_x_5 is average of df4.batsman_runs (float), target expects integer, so round
result['batsman_runs_x_5'] = result['batsman_runs_x_5'].fillna(0).round().astype(int)
result['no of balls'] = result['no of balls'].fillna(0).astype(int)
result['batsman_runs_y_7'] = result['batsman_runs_y_7'].fillna(0).astype(int)
result['strike'] = result['strike'].fillna(0).astype(float)
result['batsman_runs'] = result['batsman_runs'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema order:
result = result[['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x', 'total_runs_x', 'total_runs_y', 'batsman_runs_y',
                 'batsman_runs_x_5', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs_y_7', 'strike', 'batsman_runs']]

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_95/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
